title: Australian PM's Melon Joke Sparks Diplomatic Stir
summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's joke about a gift of Japanese melons has caused diplomatic friction. During a state dinner, Albanese reportedly joked that the melons, a gift from Japan's Prime Minister Fumio Kishida, were intended to make him "fat". The Japanese ambassador to Australia, Reiichiro Kanazawa, has stated the remark was "misunderstood" and "not a problem". However, Opposition Leader Peter Dutton claimed Albanese "stuffed up" the diplomatic gesture. The incident occurred during a state dinner attended by the Japanese Prime Minister.
summary_points: Australian PM Anthony Albanese made a joke about a gift of Japanese melons.
Albanese reportedly said the melons were meant to make him "fat".
The Japanese ambassador to Australia, Reiichiro Kanazawa, downplayed the incident, calling it a misunderstanding.
Australian Opposition Leader Peter Dutton criticized Albanese's handling of the gift.
The joke was made during a state dinner with the Japanese Prime Minister.
title_hi: ऑस्ट्रेलियाई पीएम के तरबूज मजाक से राजनयिक हलचल
summary_hi: ऑस्ट्रेलिया के प्रधानमंत्री एंथनी अल्बनीज द्वारा जापानी तरबूज उपहार पर किए गए मजाक से राजनयिक तनाव पैदा हो गया है। एक राजकीय रात्रिभोज के दौरान, अल्बनीज ने कथित तौर पर मजाक किया कि जापान के प्रधानमंत्री फुमियो किशिदा द्वारा उपहार में दिए गए तरबूज उन्हें "मोटा" बनाने के लिए थे। ऑस्ट्रेलिया में जापानी राजदूत, रेइचिरो कानाज़ावा ने कहा कि टिप्पणी को "गलत समझा गया" और "कोई समस्या नहीं" थी। हालांकि, विपक्षी नेता पीटर डटन ने दावा किया कि अल्बनीज ने राजनयिक हावभाव को "खराब कर दिया"। यह घटना जापानी प्रधानमंत्री की उपस्थिति में एक राजकीय रात्रिभोज के दौरान हुई।
